toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% with an upper normal limit of 0.482%, and 0.411% is inside that. Three earlier weeks were higher (0.44%, 0.47% and 0.51%), and investigating them found nothing. The dashboard numbers match a recount from the raw logs, and no one edited the query. Burn rate is 0.82x, well under the 2x paging threshold. Booking completion is flat (41.0% vs 41.2%), and support logged no complaints.

The "new pods error twice as much" finding is a rollout warm-up effect. New pods start with an empty cache and time out against the database. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image. It accounts for only 10–20 errors per rollout, against a weekly rise of about 2,280. The comparison never tested v4.18 against v4.17 on pods of the same age, so it says nothing about a fault in v4.18.

Recommendation: don't roll back, and don't mute alerting. Muting would remove the protection that would catch a real problem. Record the week as within the normal band and apply the standard check to next week. If next week is above 0.482%, or the burn-rate page fires, open an incident then. I am fairly confident, though I did not rule out a small real effect from the release, the replica move or partner-sync.
